title: A Taste of the Shore
paras: Food researcher Mina Okafor studies seaweed on a quiet island. Her work began when she noticed that visitors enjoyed local [[seafood|seafood]] but left the green plants on their plates. Their [[attitude|attitude]] interested her: many thought seaweed was only food for fish. Mina wanted to discover whether a simple soup could change their minds. She chose a small kitchen near the beach as the [[location|location]] for her experiment.

Each morning, Mina collected a little seaweed from an area with clean water. Back in the kitchen, she cooked it with potatoes and [[celery|celery]]. Too much seaweed left a strong salty taste on the [[tongue|tongue]], so she tested several amounts. She invited twelve island residents to taste three small bowls each. People [[tend|tend]] to give less careful answers when they [[tire|tire]], so each visit lasted only twenty minutes. Afterwards, everyone completed a short [[questionnaire|questionnaire]] about taste and smell.

The favourite soup contained just one spoonful of seaweed per bowl. With a local cook, Mina developed it into a product under their new [[brand|brand]], Shore Spoon. Each jar had a blue [[label|label]] showing the ingredients and where the seaweed grew. For Mina, the best result was not the jars themselves. It was seeing a visitor finish her soup, then ask to see the plants growing along the shore.
zh: 食品研究员米娜·奥卡福在一座宁静的小岛上研究海藻。她发现，游客很喜欢当地的海鲜，却把盘子里的绿色植物剩了下来，她的研究便由此开始。他们的看法引起了她的兴趣：许多人认为海藻只是鱼的食物。米娜想知道，一道简单的汤能否改变他们的想法。她选了海滩附近的一间小厨房作为实验地点。
每天早晨，米娜都会从一片水质洁净的区域采集少量海藻。回到厨房后，她把海藻与土豆、芹菜一起煮。海藻放得太多，舌头上就会留下很重的咸味，因此她试了几种不同的用量。她邀请了十二位岛上居民，每人品尝三小碗汤。人们疲倦时往往回答得不够认真，所以每次品尝只持续二十分钟。之后，每个人都填写了一份有关味道和气味的简短问卷。
最受欢迎的汤每碗只放一勺海藻。米娜与一位当地厨师合作，将它开发成产品，使用他们新创立的品牌“海岸一勺”。每个罐子上都贴着一张蓝色标签，注明配料和海藻的生长地点。对米娜来说，最好的成果并不是这些罐装汤本身，而是看到一位游客喝完汤后，提出想去看看生长在岸边的海藻。

q.s: Mina's research was inspired by visitors avoiding seaweed while enjoying other local food.
q.why: 她发现游客喜欢海鲜，却剩下海藻。

q.s: The island residents were paid to taste Mina's soups.
q.why: 文章未说明品尝者是否获得报酬。

q.s: The labels on the soup jars were red.
q.why: 原文明确说罐子上的标签是蓝色的。
